Beastmasters

Setting

The Beastmasters’ settlement brings together Geraldine, Crooked, Trickster and Yam-Akara. Suspicion after the empty caravan tests the newcomers’ reception. The truth about Brissen’s death ultimately exposes a crime within this community. [1, 2, 3, 4]

The Beastmasters and the empty caravan

At the Beastmasters’ settlement, Crooked accuses Kir and Kel of being spies. Geraldine agrees to test them. Their attempt to obtain a gold nugget from a caravan finds an empty chest, making their return dangerous. Trickster reasons that genuine thieves would not come back empty-handed, and Geraldine accepts them. Advice from Trickster, also passed on by Sver if Kir consults him, about an ice elemental in the abandoned mines provides something to offer Yam-Akara. His work and the governor’s permit requirements then draw the travellers into further dealings with the court. The missing nugget will matter again when the apparent caravan failure becomes evidence of a separate theft. [2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10]

Geraldine’s secret meetings

Trickster notices that Geraldine repeatedly leaves the settlement in secret. As its leader, he argues, she should not keep matters from her people. He asks Kir and Kel to follow her. They see a meeting with a man, but magical traps prevent them from approaching unnoticed and frighten the pair away. Their first report therefore establishes a secret meeting, not the man’s identity. Suspicion later falls on both His and Karansul; the eventual explanation is Geraldine’s relationship with the merchant, whom she plans to marry. [11, 12, 13]

The planted knife and His’s death

A knife found at the murder site appears to implicate His. The court magician admits it was stolen from his laboratory together with the governor’s nugget. He had sent out the empty caravan to hide that loss and hoped to blame raiders after an informant warned of the planned attack. His arranges a meeting to produce evidence, but is killed before he can clear himself. Meanwhile Geraldine and Karansul disclose their relationship and provide each other with an alibi. Their commercial hostility and private secrecy had made them suspicious without establishing guilt. [14, 15, 7, 16, 13]

Crooked’s confession

The settlement’s missing communal money supplies the decisive motive. Kir and Kel catch Crooked at his cache. Brissen had discovered the theft, so Crooked killed him. He also stole His’s knife and the gold nugget, informed on the caravan raid and later planted the knife to shift suspicion. His called the same informant to clear his own name; Crooked mistook that invitation for a trap and killed him too. Woodsfolk observations help reconstruct the planted evidence. Before the governor, Kir explains the connected crimes and Crooked admits them. Yam-Akara is released, while the governor reserves Crooked’s punishment for trial. Kel draws the thief out by spreading word that they have found the hidden money. Afterwards the travellers return the recovered communal funds to Geraldine and Trickster. Geraldine wants personal revenge, but Crooked is already in the governor’s custody. [17, 18, 19, 20, 4, 21, 22]

The hidden portal to Jigran

During his confinement, Yam-Akara gains access to the governor’s library. Old exploration reports reveal that the powerful “artifact” is a forgotten passage to another land. Trickster offers a key to the gate, then sends Kir on a fruitless ore search so that he can work without interference. With the key ready, Yam-Akara warns that he cannot sense the destination: the portal may be defective or concealed by a powerful absorbing spell. Kir recognises the same absence Tka-Rik described and concludes that it leads to Jigran. He decides to go directly, trusting the strength gained during his journey. Kel chooses to accompany him again. [21, 23, 24, 25]
